name: Kansas City International Airport

spaces.name: Quiet Room
spaces.location: Concourse A, inside an alcove near Gate 12
spaces.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week
spaces.type: quiet room (multipurpose; airport says prayer rugs welcome)

notes: Official Specialty Rooms page (https://www.flykc.com/specialty-rooms) read 18 Oct 2026 through its page data (flykc.com/page-data/specialty-rooms/page-data.json). Quote: "Our Quiet Room is a multipurpose space designed to serve anyone and everyone looking for a sense of peace while traveling. Reflect, reset, roll out a prayer rug or yoga mat, or simply escape out of the hustle and bustle of a busy terminal into a serene environment. The Quiet Room is open to ticketed passengers 24 hours a day, 7 days a week with no reservation needed. It is located in Concourse A, inside an alcove near Gate 12." 'Open to ticketed passengers' means it is past security. The page also lists a separate Sensory Room (Atrium B near Concourse B, for neurodivergent travelers), not a prayer space. Wudu facilities, a women's area and qibla marking are not described. The 2023 KCTV5 report cited earlier agrees with the location.

name: Winnipeg James Armstrong Richardson International Airport
notes: Official Services list (https://www.ywg.ca/en/passengers/at-ywg/services/) and the service page read 18 Oct 2026. The page lists "Non-Denominational Prayer Space", "Level 2", "After Security (Domestic and International)", "Open 24 hours", and says: "This interim non-denominational prayer space is intended to provide a quiet, respectful environment for reflection and prayer for individuals of all beliefs and backgrounds. Kindly keep noise to a minimum, silence electronic devices, and be considerate of those around you." 'Interim' suggests the room may move. The exact gate is not stated (the page has a map), and wudu, a women's area and qibla marking are not described.

name: Ministro Pistarini International Airport (Ezeiza)
notes: No prayer room at Ezeiza as of 18 Oct 2026. A fact-check by Chequeado (16 Sep 2026, https://chequeado.com/ultimas-noticias/no-el-aeropuerto-de-ezeiza-no-incorporo-en-2026-una-sala-de-rezo-islamica-la-sala-fue-inaugurada-en-el-2000-y-cerro-en-2025/, unverified secondary source) reports that the Islamic prayer room (sala de rezo), opened in 2000 and remodelled in 2011, has closed. It quotes Aeropuertos Argentina's press office: "La sala no está desde el año pasado" and "Estaba en una zona de obras, se está buscando un nuevo lugar" (it was in a construction zone, and a new location is being sought). Earlier official-site check, 13 Oct 2026: the EZE free-services list names Wi-Fi, coworking, carts, water refill, phone chargers, wheelchairs, self check-in and tax refund, and none of the 1,482 sitemap URLs mention a capilla or prayer room. The official site search loads by JavaScript and could not be used on 18 Oct. A 2005 Vatican list named a Catholic chapel at Ezeiza; its current status is unknown. Ask Aeropuertos Argentina whether a replacement room has opened.
